title: When the Same Problem Has Different Names
title_ja: 同じ課題に異なる名前があるとき
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の人物、学校、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: International projects often begin with a decision to address a common problem, yet agreement about a general objective does not necessarily imply agreement about the precise meaning of the problem.
sentences.ja: 国際活動は共通課題に対処する判断から始まることが多いが、一般目標の合意は課題の正確な意味の合意を必ずしも意味しない。

sentences.en: People may describe similar experiences using categories that reflect the institutions, practices and expectations of their own communities.
sentences.ja: 人々は自地域の組織、慣行、期待を反映する分類を用いて似た経験を説明する場合がある。

sentences.en: An expression that appears to be an accurate translation may therefore connect ideas that are comparable in some respects but different in others.
sentences.ja: したがって正確な訳に見える表現も、一部の点では比較可能だが他の点では異なる考えを結ぶかもしれない。

sentences.en: An imagined school exchange provides an example of how such differences can become a useful subject for international cooperation.
sentences.ja: 仮想の学校交流はこうした違いが国際協力の有用な題材になり得る例を提供する。

sentences.en: Students at two schools decide to compare the availability of places where young people can study outside normal school hours.
sentences.ja: 二校の生徒は通常授業時間外に若者が勉強できる場所の利用可能性を比較することにする。

sentences.en: Both groups use a translated expression referring to public study spaces, and each prepares a list of the places that it considers relevant.
sentences.ja: 双方が公共自習空間を指す翻訳表現を用い、関連すると考える場所の一覧を準備する。

sentences.en: When they exchange their lists, one group discovers that the other has included locations that it would usually classify as belonging to a different category.
sentences.ja: 一覧を交換すると、一方は他方が通常なら別分類に属すると見なす場所を含めたことを発見する。

sentences.en: A direct comparison of the number of locations would consequently risk comparing collections defined according to different criteria.
sentences.ja: したがって場所数の直接比較は異なる基準で定義された集合を比較する危険がある。

sentences.en: The students discuss which practical characteristics they wish to investigate.
sentences.ja: 実際のどの特性を調べたいか話し合う。

sentences.en: They identify several questions concerning access, such as whether a place is open to students who are not members of a particular organization and whether it is available at relevant times.
sentences.ja: 特定組織に所属しない生徒にも開かれるか、関連時間帯に利用可能かなどアクセスに関する問いを複数特定する。

sentences.en: Instead of requiring each group to abandon its familiar categories, they prepare a common description of the characteristics to be recorded.
sentences.ja: 各班に身近な分類を放棄するよう求めず、記録すべき特性について共通記述を作る。

sentences.en: This arrangement allows them to recognize differences in local terminology while examining information that is relevant to their shared objective.
sentences.ja: この仕組みは共通目標に関連する情報を調べつつ地域用語の違いを認識することを可能にする。

sentences.en: The groups find that discussing the meaning of their terms has become an important part of the project.
sentences.ja: 用語の意味の議論が活動の重要部分になったと班は気づく。

sentences.en: They can now explain why two locations that share a translated name might nevertheless offer different opportunities for young people.
sentences.ja: 翻訳名称が共通の二地点がそれでも若者に異なる機会を提供し得る理由を説明できる。

sentences.en: The fictional exercise does not establish the availability of study spaces in actual communities or define a universally appropriate category.
sentences.ja: 架空活動は実地域での自習空間の利用可能性を確定せず、普遍的に適切な分類も定義しない。

sentences.en: It illustrates the importance of examining the relationship between the words used in a comparison and the experiences that those words are intended to describe.
sentences.ja: 比較で用いる語とそれが記述しようとする経験との関係を調べる重要性を示す。

sentences.en: Cooperation across languages involves more than selecting equivalent expressions from a dictionary.
sentences.ja: 言語を越えた協力には辞書から同等表現を選ぶ以上のことが伴う。

sentences.en: It may require people to develop shared questions without assuming that their communities organize the world in identical ways.
sentences.ja: 地域が世界を同じ方法で整理すると想定せず共通の問いを作る必要がある場合がある。

sentences.en: The resulting differences can provide opportunities to learn about both the other community and one's own assumptions.
sentences.ja: 得られる違いは相手地域と自分自身の前提の両方について学ぶ機会を提供し得る。

sentences.en: A common purpose can become clearer through a discussion of the different words initially chosen to describe it.
sentences.ja: 共通目的は当初それを記述するため選ばれた異なる語の議論を通じてより明確になり得る。

questions.prompt: Why may agreement on an objective be insufficient?
options: The project must have only one participant.
Communities may use different categories to understand the problem.
Common objectives cannot be expressed in language.
Places for studying outside school hours.
The number of languages in each school.
The cost of building new classrooms.
The examination results of every student.

questions.prompt: Why is a direct count problematic?
options: One group is unable to count locations.
The groups may count different kinds of places.
The places are all closed permanently.
They have already agreed on identical definitions.
Access conditions and opening times relevant to students.

questions.prompt: How do they address terminology differences?
options: Require one group to abandon its vocabulary.
Use shared descriptive questions while retaining local categories.
Translate all words without discussing meaning.

questions.prompt: What becomes an important part of the project?
options: Finding the cheapest study space in every country.

questions.prompt: Why might matching names conceal real differences?
options: The groups have agreed not to record practical features.
Every location belongs to one organization.
Locations with similar names can offer different access opportunities.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の利用条件の違い。

options: Having the same meaning or value.

questions.prompt: What can differences help the students learn?
options: Both the other community's practices and their own assumptions.
That their original categories are always superior.
That translation removes the need for comparison.
A translated label guarantees the same meaning in practice.
One community's categories should always replace the other's.
International comparisons require shared questions and attention to how local terms represent experiences.
Counting locations is enough to compare every community.
questions.explanation_ja: 共通の問いと分類の文脈。

paraphrases.source: International projects often begin with a decision to address a common problem, yet agreement about a general objective does not necessarily imply agreement about the precise meaning of the problem.
paraphrases.rewrite: Agreement on a broad goal may coexist with different understandings of the problem.

paraphrases.source: When they exchange their lists, one group discovers that the other has included locations that it would usually classify as belonging to a different category.
paraphrases.rewrite: One group includes places the other would normally categorize differently.

paraphrases.source: Instead of requiring each group to abandon its familiar categories, they prepare a common description of the characteristics to be recorded.
paraphrases.rewrite: They develop shared descriptions rather than discard familiar local categories.

paraphrases.source: It may require people to develop shared questions without assuming that their communities organize the world in identical ways.
paraphrases.rewrite: They can formulate common questions without assuming identical local practices.
